Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes and challenges that come with becoming a new mother. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed, and I'm here to support you in any way I can.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be using the EPDS to help us better understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a helpful tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will give us valuable insights into how you're feeling and whether there's any support you might need.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and respected. I want you to feel safe and supported throughout our conversation. My goal is to create a non-judgmental space where you can openly share your feelings and concerns.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us explore your emotions and experiences over the past 7 days. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. Don't worry; there are no right or wrong answers. I'm here to listen and understand your perspective.

Let's get started. The first question is about how you've been feeling lately. Have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as you used to, or have you been feeling more serious and less able to enjoy things?

Honestly, I haven't been laughing as much as I used to. It feels like everything is just so overwhelming and serious all the time. I mean, I still try to enjoy the little moments with my baby, but it's just not the same. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time. Even when I do find something funny, it's hard to really feel the joy or laughter like I used to. It's like there's this weight on me that's just making everything feel more difficult. Sometimes I'll be playing with my baby, and I'll think to myself, "Oh, this is funny," but the feeling just doesn't seem to be there like it was before. It's hard to explain. I just feel really tired and drained all the time, and I guess that's affecting how much I can enjoy things. Even the things I used to love doing, like reading or watching movies, just don't seem as interesting to me right now. Does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

No... I don't think that's me, at least not lately. Like I said, I just don't feel like I'm enjoying things as much as I used to. And when I do try to laugh or find the humor in something, it feels forced. I'm just so worried about everything, especially my baby's safety, and that worry is always there, lurking in the back of my mind. It's hard to shake off and just relax. I feel like I'm constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And that makes it really hard to laugh or feel carefree like I used to. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, trying to feed my baby or change their diaper, and my mind will just start racing with all these worst-case scenarios... it's exhausting. And it makes it hard to find the funny side of things, you know.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really... I mean, I used to love looking forward to things, like planning a night out with friends or trying a new restaurant. But lately, everything just feels like a chore. I don't really find myself getting excited about things like I used to. Even things that I know I should be enjoying, like spending time with my baby, just feel like another task to check off the list. I know that sounds terrible, but it's just how I've been feeling. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, instead of actually enjoying the experience. And when I do think about doing something I used to enjoy, like reading a book or taking a walk, I just feel guilty because I think I should be spending that time with my baby instead. It's like I'm stuck in this cycle of feeling overwhelmed and guilty, and I don't know how to get out of it. Sometimes I'll think about doing something fun, and then I'll just start worrying about all the things that could go wrong, like my baby getting sick or something happening to them while I'm not paying attention... and that just kills any excitement I might have had. It's hard to explain, but it's just like the joy has been sucked out of everything for me right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that's definitely me. I feel like I'm constantly blaming myself for everything. If my baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If they're not sleeping, I think it's because I didn't establish a good routine. If they're not eating, I think it's because I'm not producing enough milk... it's just this never-ending cycle of self-doubt and blame. I feel like I'm not good enough, like I'm failing as a mother. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to burp my baby, I'll think to myself, "What a terrible mother I am, I'm so careless." Or, if I don't get the laundry done, I'll think, "I'm such a failure, I'm not even taking care of my baby's basic needs." It's like I'm my own worst critic, and it's exhausting. Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeling overwhelmed and anxious, and I'll just start thinking about all the things I've done wrong as a mother. It's like this constant barrage of negative self-talk, and it's hard to shut it off. I just wish I could be kinder to myself, you know? But it's hard when I feel like I'm just making mistake after mistake.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's me all the time. I feel like I'm constantly worried about something, even when everything seems fine. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or playing with them, and suddenly I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if my baby stops breathing? What if I drop them? What if someone breaks into the house? It's just this constant stream of worst-case scenarios playing out in my mind, and it's hard to shake off. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll worry about my baby's temperature, or whether they're eating enough, or whether they're developing properly. It's like I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? And it's exhausting. Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start thinking about all these things, and I'll get this knot in my stomach, and I'll feel like I'm going to throw up. It's hard to calm myself down, and it's hard to sleep. I just wish I could turn off my brain and just relax, but it feels like my mind is always racing. And the worst part is, it feels like there's no reason for any of it. My baby is healthy, my family is supportive, I have everything I need... but still, the worry is just always there, lurking in the back of my mind.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something completely normal, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, my hands will start shaking, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. It's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, but there's no threat there. It's just me, alone in my house, with my baby. It's so scary, because I don't know what's happening or why it's happening. And it's hard to calm myself down, because my mind is racing and I'm thinking about all the worst-case scenarios. Sometimes I'll try to breathe deeply, or I'll try to distract myself by doing something else, but it's hard to shake off the feeling of panic. It's like my body is just on high alert all the time, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes I'll be out in public, with my baby, and I'll feel this panic start to rise up. I'll be holding my baby, and I'll think, "What if someone tries to take them from me?" or "What if I trip and drop them?" It's just this constant fear, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm always walking on eggshells, waiting for something to happen. And the worst part is, I don't know how to make it stop. I just wish I could feel safe and calm, like I used to before I had my baby.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me and I don't know how to deal with it all. Being a new mom is hard, and it feels like there's just so much pressure to get everything right. And if I'm not getting everything right, then I'm a failure. It's like, I'm supposed to be this perfect mom, with the perfect baby, and the perfect house, and the perfect life... but it's just not realistic. And when things don't go according to plan, I feel like I'm just drowning in it all. Like, the other day, my baby was crying and I was trying to make dinner, and the laundry was piling up, and I just felt like I was going to lose my mind. I didn't know how to calm my baby down, or how to get everything done, or how to even take care of myself. It just felt like everything was getting on top of me, and I didn't know how to escape. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to get my baby to sleep, and I'll be feeling so tired, but then I'll think about all the things I need to do, like cleaning the house, or paying the bills, or cooking dinner... and it just feels like too much. I feel like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, but it's hard. Sometimes I'll just sit there, feeling overwhelmed, and I'll think to myself, "I don't know how much more of this I can take." It's like, I'm just trying to survive, but it's hard to see a way out of it all.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and it's not just because my baby is waking up at night. It's like, my mind is just racing all the time, and I feel so unhappy and overwhelmed that I just can't seem to wind down. I'll be lying in bed, and I'll be thinking about all the things that are stressing me out, like my baby's health, or my relationship with my partner, or just feeling like I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom... and it's hard to calm myself down. Sometimes I'll be awake for hours, just lying there, feeling anxious and worried. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these vivid dreams that are just so unsettling. Like, I'll dream that something is happening to my baby, or that I'm losing them, or that I'm just failing as a mom in some way... and it's just so disturbing. It's like, my mind is just tormenting me, even when I'm supposed to be resting. And then, of course, there's the fact that I'm just so tired all the time. Being a new mom is exhausting, and it feels like I'm just running on empty all the time. I'll be trying to take care of my baby, and I'll just feel like I'm going to collapse from fatigue. It's like, I'm just trying to survive, but it's hard when I'm not getting any rest. Sometimes I'll just sit there, feeling so tired and unhappy, and I'll think to myself, "I don't know how much more of this I can take." It's like, I'm just trying to make it through each day, but it's hard when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and anxious all the time.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, and it's hard to explain why. I mean, I know I'm supposed to be happy and excited about being a new mom, but the truth is, I just don't feel that way. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, trying to take care of my baby and do all the things I'm supposed to do, but it's just feeling so empty and unfulfilling. I'll be sitting there, holding my baby, and I'll just start crying because I feel so overwhelmed and sad. It's like, I'm just trying to hold it together, but it's hard when I feel like I'm drowning in all these emotions. Sometimes I'll be doing okay, and then something will just trigger me, like a commercial on TV or a conversation with a friend, and I'll just start sobbing. It's like, I'm just so sensitive and emotional all the time, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm just trying to survive, but it's hard when I'm feeling so sad and miserable all the time. I've even had thoughts of... of not being here, of not being a part of this world anymore. It's scary, and it's hard to admit, but it's the truth. I just feel so lost and alone, and I don't know how to make it stop. I just wish I could feel happy and fulfilled again, like I used to before I had my baby. But right now, it just feels like that's a distant memory, and I'm not sure how to get back to that place.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just start sobbing. It's not even like something specific will trigger it, it's just like my emotions will just overwhelm me and I'll start crying. Sometimes it's because I'm feeling so sad and miserable, and sometimes it's just because I'm feeling so overwhelmed and anxious. I'll be trying to take care of my baby, and I'll just start crying because I feel like I'm not doing a good enough job. Or, I'll be thinking about all the things I need to do, and I'll just feel so overwhelmed that I'll start crying. It's like, I'm just so sensitive and emotional all the time, and it's exhausting. I've cried in front of my partner, I've cried in front of my friends, I've even cried in front of strangers... it's just like, I have no control over my emotions anymore. And it's not just the crying, it's the feeling of sadness and hopelessness that comes with it. It's like, I'll be crying, and I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I just be happy and fulfilled like I'm supposed to be?" It's like, I'm just so disappointed in myself, and it's hard to shake off that feeling. Sometimes I'll try to hide my tears, but it's hard. My baby will be looking at me, and I'll be trying to smile and be happy, but inside I'll be dying. It's like, I'm just so tired of feeling this way, and I don't know how to make it stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(sobbing) Oh, yes... I'm so ashamed to admit it, but yes, those thoughts have occurred to me. It's like, I'll be feeling so overwhelmed and sad, and I'll just think to myself, "What's the point of all this? Why am I even here?" And then, these thoughts will just creep in, like, "Maybe it would be easier if I just wasn't here anymore." It's like, my mind is just trying to find a way to escape all the pain and suffering, but it's not a rational thought, I know that. It's just... it's like, I feel so trapped and alone, and I don't know how to make it stop. (cries)

I know it sounds crazy, but sometimes I'll be holding my baby, and I'll just think, "What if I'm not enough for them? What if I'm not a good enough mom?" And then, these thoughts will just start to spiral out of control, and I'll think, "Maybe it would be better for them if I just wasn't here." It's like, my mind is just trying to find a way to make everything okay, but it's not okay. It's not okay to think those thoughts, and I know that.

(pauses, taking a deep breath)

I'm so scared, because I don't know how to make these thoughts stop. I don't know how to make myself feel better. I just feel so lost and alone, and I don't know how to find my way back. (sobs) I'm sorry, I'm just so sorry. I don't know how to do this. I don't know how to be a good mom, and I don't know how to take care of myself. I just feel so broken.

5. Encourage patient to engage in self-care activities, such as exercise, meditation, and social support
